result:
The chart type gallery now also appears on the insight page in view mode, replacing the plain dropdown there. Nothing was run (per your instructions), so the change and the new test cases are untested.

## What changed

**`products/product_analytics/frontend/insights/chartAlternatives/chartAlternativesLogic.ts`**

The gallery was gated by the `isEditableSurface` selector, which required `editMode`. It now accepts either edit mode or the insight page in view mode, using the existing `isInViewMode` selector from `insightLogic`:

```ts
(!!editMode || isInViewMode) && !embedded && !inSharedMode && !isInDashboardContext && canEditInsight && !editingDisabledReason
```

**`ChartAlternatives.test.tsx`**

I added one parameterized test for rendering outside edit mode: the gallery button shows on the insight view URL and does not show on another page.

## Behavior to be aware of

- **Still gated as before:** the gallery only shows for trends insights, behind the `PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_CHART_ALTERNATIVES` flag, and for users who can edit the insight. View-only users still get the dropdown in view mode.
- **Other surfaces unchanged:** dashboards, notebooks, shared and embedded insights keep the dropdown, because I keyed on the insight page URL rather than dropping the edit mode check outright.
- **Editing unchanged:** the edit mode path evaluates exactly as it did.

## Decision for you

Should users without edit access also see the gallery in view mode? I kept the `canEditInsight` requirement because picking a chart type from the gallery changes the query, the same as in edit mode. Dropping it is a one-line change in the same selector, but then view-only users could change the chart locally without being able to save.
